questions.question:
Select the correct option of the given sentence.

Smt. Savithri is wisest than all others in the group.

options.text: Smt. Savithri is the wiser than all others in the group.
Smt. Savithri is wise than all others in the group.
Smt. Savithri is wiser than all others in the group.
Smt. Savithri is the wise than all others in the group.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '3' i.e.Smt. Savithri is wiser than all others in the group.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is comparing Smt. Savithri to all others in the group, which requires the use of a comparative adjective.
 
• Comparative adjectives are used to compare differences between two objects (or people).
 
• The correct form of the comparative adjective for "wise" is "wiser".

Correct sentence: *Smt. Savithri is wiser than all others in the group.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Comparative Adjectives:**

 
 
• **Structure:** adjective + -er (for one-syllable adjectives) or more + adjective (for adjectives with two or more syllables).
 
• **Example:** She is taller than her brother.
 
• **Usage: **Used to compare differences between two people or things.
 
 
 
• **Superlative Adjectives:**
 
 
• **Structure: **adjective + -est (for one-syllable adjectives) or most + adjective (for adjectives with two or more syllables).
 
• **Example: **She is the tallest in her class.
 
• **Usage: **Used to describe the highest degree of a quality among three or more people or things.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

He possesses one of the __slimmer__ handsets in the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. slimmest .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**one of the**" is typically followed by a **superlative adjective** and a **plural noun**. 
 
• The adjective 'slim' is a short adjective, and its superlative form is created by adding '-est' (slimmest). The comparative is 'slimmer'. 
 
• The original sentence used the comparative form "slimmer" after "one of the", which is grammatically incorrect in this context. 
 
• Therefore, the superlative form "slimmest" is required to correctly follow "one of the".

Correct sentence: *He possesses one of the **slimmest** handsets in the world*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• **Degrees of Comparison:** Adjectives have three degrees of comparison: 

 
 
• **Positive:** slim (used when describing a single item or comparing equals, e.g., "This phone is slim.") 
 
• **Comparative:** slimmer (used when comparing two items, e.g., "This phone is slimmer than that one.") 
 
• **Superlative:** slimmest (used when comparing three or more items and indicating the highest degree, e.g., "This is the slimmest phone I've seen.") 
 
 
 
• The construction "one of the" indicates that we are talking about one item from a group of items that all possess the quality to the highest degree. Thus, the superlative is necessary.
